clue.text: Lots more kids, but only a little noise?

definitions.meaning: a sudden surge in the birth rate, as after the Second World War
read literally, a bang made by an infant is a tiny explosion

explanation.surface: A puzzled parent notes that far more children are around, yet things are oddly quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A demographic surge in births is the standard name for a sharp rise in the number of children born.

clue.text: Start to read through Waugh's daily: this once on page 3?

indicators.note: through puts that letter right inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Daily Beast is the newspaper in Evelyn Waugh's novel Scoop

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of read

explanation.surface: Begin by reading through a Waugh novel's newspaper; this used to appear on page 3.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 of The Sun, a British tabloid, carried topless photographs of models until 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun's notorious page 3 featured topless models, so bare bosoms were once its fixture.

clue.text: Little to keep king leaving union

indicators.note: keep means the word for little holds the king inside it

parts.note: a bit is a little
rex is Latin for king, as on coins

explanation.surface: A small effort to keep the monarch as the union breaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's departure from the European Union got its own portmanteau name, here clued by its plain meaning.

clue.text: In Ireland, be awfully poor on this

indicators.note: awfully means the letters of Ireland and be are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A grim comment on poverty in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the line of subsistence income is the idiom for being poor.

clue.text: Safe now to serve beer so?

definitions.meaning: free of danger at last, having come through
beer drawn straight from the cask is served from the wooden barrel

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means past the danger; literally it describes ale poured from a wooden cask.

clue.text: Material is excellent, endlessly ornate

parts.note: fab is slang for excellent, short for fabulous

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for ornate loses its final letter

parts.note: rich decoration is ornate, lavish

explanation.surface: A judgement on a cloth: superb, if a touch overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth or textile is called material, the stuff a garment is made from.

clue.text: With beginnings of asthma, is reaching with hesitation for ventilator

indicators.note: beginnings of picks the opening letter of each of the three words

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An asthmatic, hesitating, reaches for a breathing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ventilator' suggests a medical machine; here it is a clothes rack that lets air at washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse airs laundry, so a drying rack is something that ventilates clothes.

clue.text: Part of day fine … stop!

parts.note: a weather forecast: one part of the day is fine, so the remainder brings showers

explanation.surface: A forecaster gives a fine spell, then a cry to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: If part of the day is fine, the REST is RAIN: the forecast's unstated other half makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back or check someone is to stop them.

clue.text: It's cold beside the road; get closer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
on can mean beside or next to, as in on the coast
the verge is the grass strip at the edge of a road

explanation.surface: It is chilly by the roadside as two things draw near.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that meet move towards one point, drawing nearer together.

clue.text: What about learner at race, perhaps well down the grid?

indicators.note: about means the exclamation for what goes round the other pieces

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard
L is the learner driver's plate
a race is one example of a sporting event

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a novice driver entered in a motor race, starting far back.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid here is a motor-racing starting grid, not the crossword's: eleventh place is well back from pole position.
explanation.definitionFit: On a racing starting grid, a starting position in double figures is well behind the front-runners.

clue.text: Prayer of saint to be set among the stars

indicators.note: set among says the saint's letter goes inside the constellation

parts.note: Orion is a well-known constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A saint's prayer destined to be placed in the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an archaic or poetic word for a prayer or supplication.

clue.text: Sluggish, not in going under old porch but on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, going under puts the sluggish part below the porch

parts.note: a veranda is an open porch

indicators.note: not in says the two letters spelling in are removed

parts.note: bovine means cow-like, slow and sluggish

explanation.surface: A lazy creature avoids going inside, staying beneath an old porch or on its roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition, besides or beyond, the sense of on top of something else.

clue.text: Observed leading Scotsmen like a piper

indicators.note: leading picks the opening letter of Scotsmen

parts.note: the Pied Piper of Hamelin wore a multicoloured, pied, coat

explanation.surface: Someone saw a piper heading a band of Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a piper' points to the Pied Piper of Hamelin, the folk-tale rat catcher in a particoloured coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy is to catch sight of or notice, so the past tense means saw or noticed.

clue.text: African grower available to engage tennis champion

indicators.note: engage means the word for available takes the champion inside it

parts.note: free means available, not engaged
Chris Evert, multiple Grand Slam winner

explanation.surface: An African farmer is free to hire a famous tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grower' looks like a farmer but is a plant: an acacia of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The fever tree is an acacia native to Africa, a plant that grows there, hence a grower.

clue.text: Musician's skill rescued tarnished gig

indicators.note: rescued suggests the gig's words are rebuilt, read as re-scued, worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician's ability saved a performance that had been going badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing music at first view from the score is a skill many performers need.

clue.text: Egyptian leader with a popular record attracts people

indicators.note: attracts means the record phrase draws the people inside it

parts.note: hot means in demand, popular
EP is an extended-play record
men means people, persons

explanation.surface: A pharaoh with a hit single draws a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of several ancient pharaohs, rulers of Egypt.

clue.text: Jack, abandoning tasks, smoked behind screen

indicators.note: abandoning means the jack is dropped from the word for tasks

parts.note: jobs are tasks
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
cured meat or fish may be preserved by smoking

explanation.surface: Jack skives off work and has a cigarette out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden behind a screen is concealed or blocked from view.

clue.text: Couple rowing: I'd come running across the street

indicators.note: across puts the shuffled letters on either side of the street
running means the letters of I'd come are set loose into a new order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Two people quarrelling; one says she is going to run across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' makes DOMEIC from I'D COME; 'across' puts that around ST.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a quarrel between partners in a household a domestic.

clue.text: Horse so sick, tamed and patted on the back

parts.note: a horse that is broken has been tamed for riding
a baby is winded by being patted on the back to bring up air

explanation.surface: A horse is ill, so it has been calmed and given a pat.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with chronic lung trouble that leaves it short of breath is described with this term.

clue.text: Ancient method of trial, or coming to agreement

parts.note: taken as written
a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: A trial either by an old ritual or by reaching a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial by ordeal, carrying red-hot iron for example, was a medieval way of judging guilt.

clue.text: Carrying burdens across back of mule that's slow

indicators.note: across means the loaded word spans the mule's final letter

parts.note: laden means loaded, carrying a burden

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of mule

explanation.surface: A mule weighed down with packs is plodding.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden describes heavy, sluggish movement, as of leaden feet.

clue.text: Drink in large amounts during music's ending

indicators.note: during means the large amounts come inside the music's ending

parts.note: a coda is the closing section of a piece of music
reams means large quantities, as in reams of paper

explanation.surface: Someone drinks heavily while the music winds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet vanilla-flavoured fizzy soft drink is the beverage meant.

clue.text: Large hill finally converted to small one

indicators.note: finally converted says the last letter of the hill word is changed into another

parts.note: a mount is a mountain or large hill

explanation.surface: A great hill ends up reduced to a hillock.
explanation.walkthrough: The final T of MOUNT becomes D.
explanation.definitionFit: A low heap of earth is a hillock, a little hill, the small one of the clue.

clue.text: Crowd keep listening

indicators.note: listening signals that the word is heard, not read

parts.note: to hoard is to keep or stockpile

explanation.surface: An order to a crowd to keep paying attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or throng of people.

clue.text: Short cut through lab maze?

definitions.meaning: a minor road drivers use to dodge main-road traffic
a maze laid out for laboratory rodents to run through

explanation.surface: A quick way through a laboratory's maze.
explanation.definitionFit: British drivers call a back street used to bypass congestion by this name; a lab rat's maze literally fits too.

clue.text: Pastoralist finds the way to part of India

parts.note: Goa is a state of India
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A herder finds the route to an Indian region.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoralist keeps grazing livestock, and a keeper of goats is one such herder.

clue.text: Resolve unfinished plan by end of year

parts.note: December, DEC, is the final month of the year

indicators.note: unfinished says the word for plan loses its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: Someone resolves a half-formed plan by the year's end.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve and to decide both mean to settle on a course or make up one's mind.

clue.text: Led follower to create flyer

definitions.meaning: the word that follows Led in the name of the rock band Led ...

explanation.surface: A guided disciple goes on to build an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid dirigible airship of the Count von Zeppelin type was a famous early flying craft.
